notes: 10 curated Astronaut Health Cards based on real published NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR / GeneLab) and NASA Human Research Program findings, written at a grade 3-6 reading level.

cards.title: Why Thick Soil Shields Cosmic Rays
cards.finding: High-energy space radiation can damage astronaut cells and DNA. Packed Moon or Mars soil (regolith) and water tanks absorb particles much better than thin metal walls.
cards.gameplayLink: Explains why sintering a 1m regolith roof and entering the Storm Shelter drastically cuts Crew Dose.
cards.sourceName: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) — Space Radiation Biology

cards.title: Bones Lose Strength in Low Gravity
cards.finding: Astronauts in weightlessness can lose ~1% of bone mineral density per month without daily resistive exercise, Vitamin D, and mineral-rich nutrition.
cards.gameplayLink: Fresh crops from your Greenhouse supply key minerals alongside crew morale.

cards.title: Muscles Need Work on Long Trips
cards.finding: When gravity is weaker (1/6 on the Moon, 3/8 on Mars), leg and back muscles shrink unless crews work out up to 2 hours every sol.
cards.gameplayLink: Keeping Life Support oxygen steady lets astronauts exercise safely without getting dizzy.

cards.title: Space Stress Affects Immune Cells
cards.finding: Comparing astronaut Scott Kelly in space to his twin Mark on Earth showed spaceflight changes how immune genes switch on and off, though most return to normal back on Earth.
cards.gameplayLink: High stress from power blackouts or radiation spikes weakens crew health faster.
cards.sourceName: NASA Twins Study / Garrett-Bakelman et al. (Science 2019)

cards.title: Fluid Shifts Change Astronaut Eyes
cards.finding: In low gravity, body fluids float upward toward the head, gently pressing on the back of the eyes (called SANS: Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome).
cards.gameplayLink: Balanced hydration in your Life Support meter helps flight surgeons monitor crew vitals.
cards.sourceName: NASA OSDR — Ocular & Fluid Shift Studies

cards.title: Red & Blue LEDs Grow Space Salad
cards.finding: ISS Veggie experiments found that red + blue LED lights help red romaine lettuce grow nutritious leaves while using far less electricity than white lamps.
cards.gameplayLink: Setting LED light cycles in the Garden Guide gives your Greenhouse a yield bonus!
cards.sourceName: NASA OSDR / ISS Veggie Plant Growth Experiments

cards.title: Roots Need Air Pockets in Microgravity
cards.finding: Too much water in space soil drowns plant roots because water sticks around roots instead of draining down. Misting (aeroponics) and wicks keep roots breathing.
cards.gameplayLink: Over-watering or ignoring Garden Guide warnings slows crop growth!
cards.sourceName: NASA OSDR — Spaceflight Root Hypoxia Studies

cards.title: Water Tanks Are Secret Radiation Shields
cards.finding: Hydrogen-rich materials like water and polyethylene plastic block fast solar protons without creating messy secondary radiation inside metal hulls.
cards.gameplayLink: Your Subterranean Storm Shelter lines crew bunks with water tanks for 96% shielding.
cards.sourceName: NASA OSDR — High-Z Particle & Proton Dosimetry

cards.title: 14-Day Nights Confuse Crew Body Clocks
cards.finding: On the Moon or Mars, strange sunrise times disrupt circadian rhythms. Tunable LED cabin lighting helps astronauts sleep deeply and stay sharp during emergencies.
cards.gameplayLink: Maintaining Habitat power preserves sleep lighting and crew decision readiness.

cards.title: Clean Air & Recycled Water Need Microbe Checks
cards.finding: Astronauts recycle up to 95-98% of cabin water and sweat! Helpful filters keep harmless microbes balanced so pipes do not clog.
cards.gameplayLink: Explains why ECLSS Water & O2 Recyclers need periodic maintenance and power.
